::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Roots, polynomials and equality breaking](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3534255/roots-polynomials-and-equality-breaking), asked by [Anon21](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/188569/anon21) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2020-02-04; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Suppose I have
>
> $$z=(a+ib)\implies z^2=(a+ib)^2\implies z=\pm(a+ib)$$
>
> But if I do this instead:
>
> $$\begin{align}
> z&=a+bi\\
> \implies z^2&=a^2-b^2+2iab\\
> &=a(2a+2ib-a)-b^2\\
> &=a(2z-a)-b^2\\
> z^2-2az+a^2+b^2&=0\\
> &\implies z=a\pm ib
> \end{align}$$
>
> Why the contradiction?
:::

There is no contradiction.  In the first derivation, you have shown that if $z=a+ib$, then either $z=a+ib$ or $z=-a-ib$.  That is true, because $z=a+ib$.

In the second, you have shown that if $z=a+ib$, then either $z=a+ib$ or $z=a-ib$.  That is true, because $z=a+ib$.
